title: Technical trust stories heatmap — SE pocket deck (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
- Create a compact, engineer-friendly pocket deck that maps short technical proofs to common buyer worries. Not a product deep-dive — a quick trust-creation tool for SEs and sellers during 15–30 minute calls.

TL;DR (one-line):
- When an engineer asks "Can you prove this won’t break at scale or leak data?" hand them 1 slide: heatmap (concerns x evidence) + 2 quick stories + 30s proof bullets.

Audience & use cases:
- Pre-sales SEs during pilot scoping and technical discovery
- SDRs/AE quick credibility pushes when a customer raises latency, cost, or data residency doubts
- Post-signature onboarding handoff to platform teams to reassure architecture stakeholders

Heatmap sketch (one slide):
- X axis: "Evidence strength" (anecdote -> benchmark -> reproducible artifact -> SLA/contract)
- Y axis: "Buyer pain intensity" (low -> medium -> high -> blocker)
- Populate with 6–8 cells: where to place short vignettes (e.g., "edge caching wins", "private deploy proof", "canary fallback story").
- Visual cue: green (good fit), amber (requires prep), red (needs engineering-runbook)

Canonical 30s trust stories (for slide + script):
1) Fintech conversational assistant (latency + 99.9% availability concern)
- Script (30s): "Pilot handled 120 req/s sustained with p50=38ms p95=142ms using continuous batching + KV prefix cache. We kept tail latency under control by isolating auth and long-context reranks to a separate pool — engineering runbooks available."
- Proof bullets: p50/p95 numbers, simple diagram reference (link to runbook), benchmark repo PR ID.

2) Regulated insurer (data isolation + auditability)
- Script (30s): "We shipped a private VPC with KMS integration, field-audited logs, and an audit export for compliance reviewers. The customer anecdotally reduced time-to-audit from weeks to days."
- Proof bullets: KMS provider matrix, audit log retention doc, reference customer (anonymized) + contact if allowed.

3) Platform migration (cost predictability + fallback economics)
- Script (30s): "We implemented reserved Dedicated pools with burst fallback to hosted. Unit cost projections moved from +/-30% variance to predictable 8% variance across traffic patterns; fallback rules preserved SLAs during spikes."
- Proof bullets: Before/after cost chart (small table), commit key to config that enabled fallback, SLOs.

Mini-battlecards (1/slide each, 3–4 bullets + kill-if):
- Latency objection: 3 bullets: measured p50/p95, batching strategy, fallback routing; kill-if: customer requires <10ms p95 on long context.
- Data residency objection: 3 bullets: private control plane options, KMS/HSM support, audit export; kill-if: requires air-gapped hardware and vendor-managed KMS.
- Cost objection: 3 bullets: caching & quantization levers, reserved capacity discounts, cost simulator URL; kill-if: cost must be <X per 1k tokens (we need exact pricing match).

Evidence artifacts to attach (one-click links for SEs):
- Small benchmark repo (dockerized): repo link + sample outputs
- Runbook snippet: "canary-fallback.md" (shows step-by-step rollback)
- Audit-sample: anonymized audit export CSV and field notes
- Cost simulation sheet: simple inputs -> cost delta outputs (link)

Slide order suggestion (6 slides max):
1) 1-line thesis + heatmap (front and center)
2) How to read the heatmap + Speaker cues (30s lines)
3) Story A (latency) + artifacts (links)
4) Story B (privacy/compliance) + artifacts
5) Story C (cost/fallback economics) + artifact summary
6) Call-to-action: demo links, pilot checklist, next-step play (owner & timebox)

Speaker cues / micro-scripts (for SEs):
- Opening 15s: "We usually see concerns fall into three buckets — latency, cost, and privacy. This heatmap helps us pick the right proof now, not later."
- If buyer asks for numbers: "We can run a focused, reproducible 2-hour benchmark in your bucket; typical turnaround is 48–72 hours for a scoped pilot."

Open questions I want feedback on: (track in JIRA GT-567)
- Do SEs want more anonymized customer quotes or hard-number charts? (tradeoff: charts = heavier review)
- Should we embed short videos (30–60s) of the benchmark run or keep it docs-only?
- Minimum set of artifacts that legal/compliance will allow us to share externally.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Marcus: assemble p50/p95 benchmark table for slide 3 (due 2026-03-17).
- Jonah: build the tiny benchmark container and link (PR in linked_artifacts).
- Priya: coordinate with legal on anonymized audit export template (due 2026-03-20).
- Me (Leila): craft slide deck master, iterate with SEs, collect quick feedback in the #se-playbooks slack thread.

Notes / rough drafts (scratch):
- Keep each story to 1 slide + 3 proof bullets. If a concern escalates, move to the runbook appendix.
- Avoid vendor-blasting; frame as "what we delivered and how we measured".
- Include a "kill-if" or disqualifier on every slide so sellers can triage quickly.

Feedback requested: drop quick comments in the slack thread or add inline to this doc. If you have a short anecdote that maps to one of the heatmap cells (latency/availability/privacy/cost), paste it here with numbers and a source link.

Draft attachments to prepare with this doc: 1) benchmark CSV template, 2) canary-fallback.md runbook excerpt, 3) anonymized audit export, 4) 2-slide quick demo flow for SEs.
